newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 9.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:

** Despite the recent monetary policy directives to contain lending rates within a four percent band above the prime lending rates, banks have been breaching this by extending loans to corporates at rates above this band, the Economic Times says.

** Indian banks are revising downwards their internal revenue and profit projections following the Reserve Bank of India diktat to adhere to an interest spread of 4.0 percent over the prime lending rate, the Business Standard reports.

** The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has convened a meeting on Tuesday to discuss the depressed capital market. The board is expected to lift a temporary ban on rights issues of mutual funds.
** Premier Automobiles Ltd posted a net loss of 270.8 billion rupees for the six months ended September 30, 1996, compared to a net profit 83.5 million rupees in the year- ago period.
** A cut in supply of natural gas by the Oil and Natural Gas Corp may cause a domestic urea production shortfall of about 200,000 tonnes, Business Standard reports.
Several firms such as Indo-Gulf Fertilisers are dependant on ONGC's natural gas for feedstock.

** The government is unlikely to consider a representation by domestic DMT producers IPCL and and Bombay Dyeing to impose anti-dumping duty on imports on polyester input PTA (purified terephthalic acid), newspapers say
** The Indian rupee opened at 35.79/80 per dollar and was seen gaining in the absence of signficant dollar demand.

** The benchmark 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed at 2,826.20 points on Friday, up from the previous close of 2,812.22. The index, which has fallen about 33 percent from its peak in June, ended the week down a hefty 64.30 points, or 2.22 percent over last week, at 2,826.20.
